Landing.tagline: Start with just one wallet address
Landing.heroBody: Smooth wallet payments for stores. The merchant shows a QR with the amount baked in, and the customer just scans and signs. Cross-chain USDC payments arrive automatically too.
Landing.heroVisualAlt: Illustration of a customer paying by scanning a QR code at a shop counter while the merchant tablet shows payment received
Landing.ctaScanBody: Connect a wallet, scan a merchant QR, and pay instantly.
Landing.ctaCreateBody: Just enter a recipient address and amount — generates a printable payment QR.
Landing.wipNote: Feature highlights, market info, transaction history, and external services will be added in upcoming updates.
Landing.featuresSubtitle: No sign-up, no custody. A payment experience that needs nothing more than a wallet.
Landing.featuresGaslessBody: When the merchant picks gasless mode while building the QR, OpenPay covers the network fee on the merchant's receive chain. Customers can pay with just JPYC / USDC — no POL or ETH needed. For cross-chain payments from a different source chain, the source chain's network fee is still paid by the customer.
Landing.featuresMultichainBody: Receive JPYC on Polygon / Kaia, USDC on Base / Arbitrum / Optimism / Polygon / Ethereum / Avalanche. Circle CCTP V2 handles cross-chain USDC payments automatically.
Landing.featuresNoncustodyBody: Funds flow straight to the merchant's wallet — OpenPay never holds your balance. No server-side ledger means no withdrawal approvals.
Landing.howItWorksSubtitle: Three steps each, for both the receiving and paying side.
Landing.howItWorksVisualAlt: Diagram showing a merchant creating a payment QR, a customer scanning it, and funds arriving in the merchant wallet
Landing.howItWorksMerchantStep2: Pick the amount, token and chain
Landing.howItWorksMerchantStep3: Print the QR for the register, or show it from a phone / tablet screen
Landing.howItWorksCustomerStep1: Connect a wallet from the top-right "Connect"
Landing.howItWorksCustomerStep2: <scan>Scan</scan> the merchant QR at the register
Landing.faqA1: In gasless mode, customers don't need POL or ETH — they pay with just their JPYC or USDC balance (that's what "gasless" means here). For JPYC payments, OpenPay advances the gas via Pimlico's paymaster and collects an equivalent amount in JPYC; whether that gas-equivalent is added on top of the customer's bill or absorbed by the merchant is chosen by the merchant when building the QR. For USDC payments, the customer pays gas in USDC to the paymaster, so OpenPay does not collect a separate gas-equivalent.
Landing.faqQ2: Can I receive both JPYC and USDC?
Landing.faqA2: Yes. JPYC is a good fit when you want JPY-denominated receipts; USDC is better for Web3-savvy or international customers. JPYC (JPY-pegged) is supported on Polygon and Kaia; USDC on Base / Arbitrum / Optimism / Polygon / Ethereum / Avalanche. Pick the chain in the QR builder. If the customer holds the token on a different chain, Circle CCTP V2 settles cross-chain automatically.
Landing.faqQ3: What if the customer has no wallet?
Landing.faqA3: Direct them to a browser wallet (MetaMask, Rabby, etc.) or a mobile wallet (MetaMask Mobile / Rainbow / Coinbase Wallet). OpenPay auto-detects multiple wallets via EIP-6963.
Landing.faqQ4: How do I convert JPYC / USDC to JPY?
Landing.faqA4: JPYC redeems 1:1 at <jpycEx>JPYC EX</jpycEx>. USDC can be sold via SBI VC Trade and other Japanese exchanges. The bottom of the <create>Receive</create> page lists exchange links per token.
Landing.faqA5: History is kept only in your browser's LocalStorage — never sent to OpenPay servers. You can export to CSV from the history page. Transaction hashes are recorded so you can verify on Etherscan / Polygonscan.
Landing.faqA6: OpenPay does not take a transaction fee tied to the payment amount — this is true today and a permanent commitment. The overall service is free during the alpha period; future monetization is being explored as a volume-independent model — a monthly subscription or a prepaid usage license (NFT pass, time-limited rights).
Landing.trustBody: OpenPay is built on a non-custodial design (funds are never held by OpenPay) and open-source stablecoin payment technology. All source code is MIT-licensed and public on GitHub — anyone can verify how the payment flow works.
Landing.trustTechStack: Tech stack: ERC-4337 (account abstraction) / ERC-7702 (EOA → smart account delegation) / Pimlico bundler/paymaster / permissionless.js / viem / wagmi
Landing.supportBody: OpenPay will never charge a payment fee tied to the transaction amount (a percentage fee). The overall service is free during the alpha period; future monetization is being explored as a volume-independent model such as a monthly subscription or usage license for peripheral features.
Landing.supportTipRequest: If you'd like to help keep OpenPay running, a tip is hugely appreciated. You can support us from the buttons below (also handy for a quick try).
Landing.benefitsSubtitle: Real value for merchants, simplicity for customers.
Landing.benefitsFeeBody: OpenPay does not take any percentage of your transaction amount. Unlike credit cards (~3%) or typical QR payment services (1.5–3.25%), there is no payment fee — no matter how large the payment is.
Landing.benefitsCostBody: No POS terminal, no contracts, no upfront fees. Just one wallet address — go from start to a printed QR the same day.
Landing.benefitsSettlementBody: Sales land in the merchant wallet the moment the on-chain transaction confirms. No month-end closing, no 2–3 business day waits (non-custodial: OpenPay never holds funds).
Landing.benefitsNoSignupBody: Customers pay with just a wallet — no address, phone or email registration required. No KYC either.
Landing.benefitsWhyLead: Wallet transfers are handy for people who can already send crypto, but they fall short as store payments: you type the recipient and amount by hand, you can pick the wrong chain or token, the store can't easily confirm what a payment is for, and you need a separate token for gas. OpenPay is an open-source payment tool that removes the friction of using wallet transfers at the point of sale.
Landing.benefitsWhyPoint1Body: The store bakes the payment conditions into a QR up front, and the customer just scans it. No hand-typing the recipient, amount, chain or token — so the slip-ups that plague raw wallet transfers go away.
Landing.benefitsWhyPoint2Body: Set a preset or any billed amount and present a clear "pay this amount" QR. Customers don't enter the amount themselves, which makes it practical at a counter or an event.
Landing.useCasesSubtitle: From merchant payments to creator support and community ops.
Landing.useCase1Body: Show one QR at a real store, flea market, or event booth — receive JPYC / USDC instantly. No POS terminal, no contract.
Landing.useCase1ImageAlt: Illustration of a cafe or event booth counter with a QR payment stand and merchant tablet
Landing.useCase2Body: Direct wallet-to-wallet payments at ETHTokyo, Devcon, and other Web3 conferences and meetups.
Landing.useCase2ImageAlt: Illustration of a Web3 conference merchandise booth where an attendee pays with a wallet
Landing.useCase3Body: Embed the Tip widget (single-line iframe) on blogs, portfolios, or stream pages — receive JPYC / USDC tips from fans.
Landing.useCase3ImageAlt: Illustration of a creator desk showing a tip widget and completed supporter payment
Landing.useCase4Body: Simplify DAO member fees, community sponsorships, and recurring collections with a single QR. On-chain receipts persist.
Landing.useCase4ImageAlt: Illustration of a community operations table sharing a QR code for membership dues
Landing.useCase5Body: Start same-day micropayments for exhibitions, pop-ups, or pubs — no contracts or POS hardware required. Viable at price points where credit cards aren't economic.
Landing.useCase5ImageAlt: Illustration of a pop-up store product table where a shopper scans a QR code for a small payment

gasHint.title: When you have no gas (POL / ETH) to send tokens to an exchange
gasHint.body: Sending received JPYC / USDC to an exchange requires a small amount of native gas on each chain (POL on Polygon, ETH on Base / Arbitrum / Optimism). With MetaMask's Swap (Gas Station) feature, you can swap on Polygon / Base / Arbitrum without holding any POL or ETH — the gas fee is paid out of your JPYC or USDC. On chains where Gas Station is not available (e.g. Optimism), a small amount of ETH is required separately to initiate the swap.
gasHint.disclaimer: Note: Availability, supported chains, and success of MetaMask features depend on MetaMask itself; OpenPay is not involved. Network congestion or unsupported token routes on any chain may cause the swap to fail.

PaymentForm.title: OpenPay Payment
PaymentForm.standardModeBody: This QR uses standard payment (with gas) mode. You need {nativeToken} (native gas token) in your wallet. OpenPay does not sponsor gas. The payment is a single transfer — approve it once in your wallet.
PaymentForm.merchantGasHint: Merchant absorbs the network fee. You pay only the displayed amount.
PaymentForm.standardBatchHint: Standard payment: approve a single transfer in your wallet. Smart Account / Pimlico Paymaster is not used.
PaymentForm.gaslessBatchHintJpyc: The network fee is charged at a fixed upper-bound (congestion ceiling) price; any surplus is not refunded (paid in JPYC).
PaymentForm.gaslessBatchHintUsdc: Upper-bound estimate. Actual gas is at or below this amount (paid in USDC).
PaymentForm.gasInfoUsdc: Pay the network fee in USDC via Pimlico ERC20 Paymaster — no need to hold native {nativeToken}. The figure shown is a worst-case estimate; any surplus over the actual cost is not charged.
PaymentForm.gasInfoUsdcCircle: Pay the network fee in USDC via Circle Paymaster (official) — no need to hold native {nativeToken}. A Circle fee of about 10% is added on top of the gas cost. The figure shown is an upper-bound estimate; any surplus is not charged. OpenPay does not collect this fee.
PaymentForm.gasInfoJpyc: Pimlico Sponsorship Paymaster covers {nativeToken} gas; you complete the payment in JPYC alone with no native ({nativeToken}) holdings required. The network fee is charged as a fixed amount based on the congestion ceiling price, so during normal periods it may exceed the actual gas (the difference is not refunded).
PaymentForm.splitBatchHint: Gas is covered by OpenPay (Pimlico Sponsorship Paymaster). {count} transfers are batched in a single UserOperation.

PaymentForm.errorReverted: The transaction reverted on-chain (no funds were transferred). Check your balance and network, then try again.
PaymentForm.gasInfoJpycRelay: For JPYC gasless payments, OpenPay advances the network fee (gas) in full. You complete the payment in JPYC alone — no native token holdings required. Just sign the transfer in your wallet.
PaymentForm.gaslessBatchHintJpycRelay: OpenPay advances the network fee, so there is no charge to you (paid in JPYC, signature only).

Terms.title: Terms of Service
Terms.intro: These Terms of Service (the "Terms") govern your use of the blockchain payment service "{service}" (the "Service") operated by {company} (the "Company"). By using the Service, you agree to be bound by these Terms.

article1.title: Article 1 (Application)
article1.body: These Terms apply to all relationships between users and the Company concerning the use of the Service. If the Company separately establishes individual rules on the Service, such individual rules form part of these Terms; in case of conflict, individual rules prevail.

article2.title: Article 2 (Definitions)
article2.body: (1) "Merchant" means a business or individual who receives Supported Token payments through the Service. (2) "Customer" means a person who pays a Merchant through the Service. (3) "Wallet" means a self-custodial crypto wallet (EOA or smart contract account) controlled by the user. (4) "Supported Token" means a digital asset supported by the Service, currently including JPYC, an electronic payment instrument issued by JPYC Inc. as a funds transfer service provider registered under Japan's Payment Services Act, and USDC, a stablecoin issued by Circle Internet Financial, Inc. (5) "Network Fee" means gas required to confirm a blockchain transaction. (6) "Gasless Payment" means a payment mode in which the Customer can complete payment without separately holding a native token (POL, ETH, etc.), and includes (a) paths where the Company sponsors the Network Fee using an ERC-4337 Paymaster or similar (e.g. JPYC payments), and (b) paths where the Customer pays the Network Fee in a Supported Token via an ERC-4337 ERC20 Paymaster (e.g. USDC payments). (7) "Standard Payment (with Gas)" means a payment mode in which the Company does not sponsor the Network Fee and the Customer pays it from their own wallet.

article3.title: Article 3 (Nature of the Service)
article3.body: The Service is a non-custodial tool that facilitates transfers of Supported Tokens between user wallets. The Company never holds user funds. All transfers are executed on-chain via the user's own signature. The Company does not issue or operate the Supported Tokens, the underlying blockchains, or the wallet applications used by users. The Service consists of generating EIP-681 payment URIs, QR codes, batching user operations under the ERC-4337 standard, and relaying gas sponsorship; the Company does not intermediate in the underlying user-to-user transaction itself. The Company does not receive, hold, manage, or later settle the price of goods, service fees, or other sales proceeds payable from Customer to Merchant. In a payment through the Service, the price of goods and similar amounts are transferred directly from the Customer's wallet to the Merchant's designated wallet. In addition, in Gasless Payment paths where the Company sponsors the Network Fee (gas) via an ERC-4337 Paymaster or similar (e.g. JPYC payments), a Network-Fee-equivalent (a fixed amount based on the congestion-ceiling price; see Article 5) is transferred separately from the Customer's wallet to a wallet designated by the Company (if the Merchant elects to bear it, the Merchant's received amount is reduced by that equivalent). In paths where the Customer pays the Network Fee in a Supported Token (e.g. the ERC20 Paymaster for USDC), that fee is paid to the Paymaster provider and no transfer is made to a wallet designated by the Company. The OpenPay service fee is currently 0%, but if such a fee is introduced in the future it will be transferred from the Customer's wallet to a wallet designated by the Company. For transactions made in Standard Payment (with Gas) mode, the Company does not sponsor the Network Fee; the Customer pays it from their own wallet. The handling of gas in any of the above paths is a feature of the Service and does not constitute custody or management of user assets by the Company.

article4.title: Article 4 (Usage Environment)
article4.body: Users are responsible for preparing, at their own cost and risk, a compatible wallet, internet connection, token balance, and (when using Standard Payment (with Gas) mode or any other path where the Company does not sponsor gas) gas in the native token. Supported chains and tokens may be added, changed, or suspended at the Company's discretion without prior notice.

article5.title: Article 5 (Fees)
article5.body: (1) The Company provides payment processing, merchant QR code generation, the checkout UI, amount/token/network selection, supported wallet integration, and operation and maintenance of the Service. The OpenPay service fee is free (0% of each transaction amount) during the alpha period. The Company does not charge any fee tied to the transaction amount (a percentage fee proportional to the amount). (2) In Gasless Payment paths where the Company sponsors the Network Fee (gas) via an ERC-4337 Paymaster or similar, or relays it as a technical advance via EIP-3009 (e.g. JPYC payments), as recovery of the advanced gas the Company collects an amount equivalent to the Network Fee from the user in JPYC or similar. In the EIP-3009 relay-advance path, the Company first advances the gas, relays the user's signed transfer authorization, and—via a contract designated by the Company (a forwarder)—performs the transfer to the Merchant and the recovery of that Network-Fee-equivalent in the same transaction, immediately. Other than collecting that Network-Fee-equivalent, the Company charges no fee or other consideration on the transaction amount. That collected amount is calculated as a fixed amount based on the upper-bound (congestion-ceiling) price and is not tied to the transaction amount; it is collected from the Customer or the Merchant according to the Merchant's configuration (if the Merchant bears it, it is deducted from the Merchant's received amount). In paths where the Customer pays the Network Fee in a Supported Token (e.g. the ERC20 Paymaster for USDC), that fee is paid to the Paymaster provider and the Company does not collect it. (3) In Standard Payment (with Gas) mode, the Company does not sponsor the Network Fee; the Customer pays the Network Fee in the native token from their own wallet. (4) Transfers from the user's wallet to a wallet designated by the Company (including the Network-Fee-equivalent in (2)) are not deducted by the Company from Merchant sales proceeds; they are sent on-chain directly from the user's wallet to a wallet or contract (forwarder) designated by the Company, and that contract distributes the received funds to the Merchant and a Company-designated wallet within the same transaction. The Company does not receive, hold, manage, or later settle the price of goods, service fees, or other sales proceeds payable from Customer to Merchant. (5) The actual Network Fee (gas) varies with blockchain congestion, underlying asset prices, third-party infrastructure specifications, and other factors. The amount collected under (2) is a fixed amount based on the congestion-ceiling price and is not intended as a pass-through of actual costs. The Company will not seek additional payment, refund, or settle any difference between the collected amount and the actual gas incurred (including any surplus where the collected amount exceeds actual cost), unless the Company expressly states otherwise. (6) In Gasless Payment mode, the Merchant may, at the time of QR code issuance, be able to elect whether the Network-Fee-equivalent is borne by the Customer or by the Merchant. If the Customer is selected, the Customer pays the Network-Fee-equivalent in addition to the price of goods. If the Merchant is selected, the Customer pays only the price of goods, and the Merchant bears the Network-Fee-equivalent. (7) The fee schedule, fees (the Company is considering future models that are not tied to the transaction amount, such as a monthly subscription or usage-license sales), supported tokens, supported chains, payment modes, and the availability and conditions of gas sponsorship may be changed at the Company's discretion. (8) For a Supported Token, if a method with a clearer network-fee structure becomes available (such as a native paymaster for that token), the Company may migrate from the technical relay-advance method above to that method.

article6.title: Article 6 (Irreversibility of Transactions)
article6.body: On-chain transactions executed through the Service cannot be cancelled, refunded, or modified due to the technical nature of blockchain. Users must verify the destination address, amount, token, chain, and payment mode before submitting. The Company is not liable for losses caused by mistransfers or incorrect inputs.

article7.title: Article 7 (Prohibited Acts)
article7.body: Users must not: (1) violate laws or public order; (2) engage in money laundering, terrorism financing, fraud, or trade in drugs, weapons, or child sexual abuse material; (3) transact with persons or regions under international economic sanctions; (4) infringe the rights of the Company, other users, or third parties; (5) perform unauthorized access, excessive load, modification, or reverse engineering of the Service; (6) use the Service if affiliated with anti-social forces; or (7) engage in any other acts the Company deems inappropriate.

article8.title: Article 8 (Third-Party Services)
article8.body: The Service depends on third-party providers including Pimlico Labs Inc., Alchemy Insights Inc., Vercel Inc., JPYC Inc., Circle Internet Financial, Inc., and various wallet application providers. The Company makes no warranty regarding availability, performance, security, pricing, or terms of these third-party services, and is not liable for losses arising from them.

article9.title: Article 9 (Disclaimer of Warranties and Limitation of Liability)
article9.body: (1) The Service is provided "as is" without any warranty of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, uninterrupted availability, or freedom from errors or vulnerabilities. (2) The Company is not liable for any damages arising from use or inability to use the Service, except in cases of the Company's intentional misconduct or gross negligence. Where the user qualifies as a consumer under Japanese consumer protection law, any clause that would fully exempt the Company from liability shall not apply, and the Company's liability cap shall be the greater of (a) JPY {amount} or (b) the total amount paid by such user to the Company in connection with the Service during the six months preceding the relevant incident (including the OpenPay service fee and any Network-Fee-equivalent collected in Gasless Payment mode). (3) The Company is not liable for losses caused by blockchain network failures, reorganizations, forks, token price volatility, gas spikes, third-party service outages, or regulatory changes.

article10.title: Article 10 (Amendment of Terms)
article10.body: Pursuant to Article 548-4 of the Japanese Civil Code (amendment of standard terms), the Company may amend these Terms when the amendment is beneficial to users in general, or when the amendment is reasonable considering the necessity, content, and circumstances of the change. Amendments take effect when the revised Terms and the effective date are posted on the Service. Continued use after the effective date constitutes acceptance of the amended Terms.

article11.title: Article 11 (Governing Law and Jurisdiction)
article11.body: These Terms and all matters relating to the Service are governed by the laws of Japan. The Tokyo District Court shall have exclusive jurisdiction as the court of first instance for any disputes arising in connection with the Service.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.intro: {company} (the "Company") establishes this Privacy Policy (the "Policy") regarding the handling of personal information in connection with the blockchain payment service "{service}" (the "Service"), in compliance with the Act on the Protection of Personal Information of Japan (the "APPI") and related laws.

section1.title: 1. Information We Collect
section1.body: We collect the following information in connection with the Service: (1) blockchain wallet addresses that the Company observes when users connect their wallet to the Service; (2) server log information including browser information, IP address, referrer, access timestamps, and page navigation; (3) anonymized statistics collected by Vercel Analytics, such as page views, visitor country/region, and device type; (4) email address and inquiry content when users contact us; (5) on-chain transaction information generated or referenced through the Service (such as transaction hash, sender wallet address, recipient wallet address, supported token, supported chain, transfer amount, OpenPay service fee, payment mode, and payment status); (6) if the user grants camera permission on pages such as /scan for QR code reading, the camera video frames and the decoded QR string. Some of this information is publicly recorded on the blockchain and may not be deletable or hideable by the Company. We may use cookies or local storage, but currently do not assign cookie identifiers that directly identify individual users.

section2.title: 2. Purposes of Use
section2.body: We use collected information for: (1) providing, operating, maintaining, and improving the Service; (2) responding to user inquiries; (3) statistical analysis and Service improvement; (4) detecting and preventing fraud, abuse, and unauthorized access; (5) responding to legal obligations; (6) other purposes ancillary to the above; (7) confirming payment status, calculating the OpenPay service fee, executing gas sponsorship in Gasless Payment mode, detecting fraud, and handling inquiries and incident investigations; (8) camera frames on pages such as /scan are processed entirely within the user's browser to decode the QR code and are never transmitted to the Company's servers or any external destination, nor are they stored. Of the decoded results, only the OpenPay payment URL category that the Service recognizes (pay / tip / checkout / external / eip681 / unknown) is sent to Sentry as an error-observation breadcrumb; the raw QR string and the user's wallet address are not sent to Sentry.

section3.title: 3. Sharing with Third Parties and Service Providers
section3.body: We do not share personal information with third parties without user consent or where required by law. However, we engage the following service providers to operate the Service, all of which we supervise as required by the APPI: - Vercel Inc. (United States): hosting, CDN, analytics. - Pimlico Labs Inc. (United States): ERC-4337 bundler and paymaster service. - Circle Internet Financial, Inc. (United States): Circle Paymaster (ERC-4337 paymaster) service for USDC gasless payments. The customer pays the gas-equivalent amount in USDC to that paymaster; the Company does not collect or receive that fee. - Alchemy Insights Inc. (United States): blockchain RPC. Because these providers are located in the United States, personal information may be transferred to a third party located in a foreign country (APPI Article 28). Information on the personal data protection regime in the United States is published by the Personal Information Protection Commission of Japan in its "Survey on Foreign Personal Information Protection Regimes." We have data protection agreements in place with these providers and have implemented measures to protect users' rights and interests.

section4.title: 4. Retention Period
section4.body: We retain collected information only for the period necessary to fulfill the purposes of use. Server logs are deleted in sequence 90 days after collection. Inquiry records are deleted 3 years after the last correspondence. On-chain transaction records, by their nature, are permanently public outside our control, and we cannot delete them.

section5.title: 5. Requests for Disclosure, Correction, and Suspension of Use
section5.body: Users may request disclosure, correction, addition, deletion, suspension of use, erasure, or suspension of third-party provision of their personal information held by us, pursuant to APPI Articles 33 through 35. For request procedures and fees, please contact us at the address shown in Section 6. We may require identity verification before responding.

section6.title: 6. Contact
section6.body: For inquiries regarding this Policy or requests under APPI: Operator: {company}. Address: {address}. Personal Information Manager: {representative}. Email: {email}.

section7.title: 7. Amendments to this Policy
section7.body: We may amend this Policy in response to changes in law, changes to the Service, or other necessary reasons. Amended Policies take effect when posted on the Service.

Privacy.legalNote: The Japanese version of this Policy prevails. This English version is provided for reference only.

Disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
Disclaimer.intro: This Disclaimer sets out the risks of using the blockchain payment service "{service}" (the "Service") operated by {company} (the "Company") and the matters for which the Company assumes no responsibility. Please read this Disclaimer together with the Terms of Service before using the Service. OpenPay does not hold customer payments or merchant sales proceeds. The price of goods and similar amounts are transferred directly to the merchant's wallet, and only the Network-Fee-equivalent in Gasless Payment where the Company sponsors gas (e.g. JPYC payments) — and the OpenPay service fee, if such a fee is introduced in the future — is transferred separately to a wallet designated by the Company.

section1.title: 1. As-Is Provision
section1.body: The Service is provided "as is." The Company makes no express or implied warranty as to the accuracy, completeness, usefulness, fitness for a particular purpose, continuous availability, freedom from errors or vulnerabilities, or absence of malicious code in the Service.

section2.title: 2. Irreversibility of Blockchain Transactions
section2.body: Transactions executed through the Service (transfers, token exchanges, and other on-chain actions) cannot be cancelled, refunded, or modified due to the technical nature of blockchain. The Company is not liable for losses caused by user operational errors such as wrong destination addresses, wrong amounts, or wrong chains. Users must verify all details before submitting.

section3.title: 3. Third-Party Issued Tokens
section3.body: JPYC is an electronic payment instrument (a JPY-denominated stablecoin) issued by JPYC Inc. as a funds transfer service provider registered under Japan's Payment Services Act; USDC is a stablecoin issued by Circle Internet Financial, Inc. Each Supported Token is issued and operated by a third-party issuer independent of the Company. The price, liquidity, availability, technical soundness, financial condition of the issuer, and regulatory compliance of each token (including maintenance of issuer registration and performance of redemption obligations) are the responsibility of the respective issuer, not the Company.

section4.title: 4. Network Fee Volatility
section4.body: Network fees (gas) are required for on-chain transactions and vary significantly with network congestion, underlying asset prices, and other factors outside the Company's control. In Gasless Payment mode, the gas estimates shown by the Service are best-effort estimates at the time of display and actual amounts may exceed them. In Standard Payment (with Gas) mode, the Customer pays the Network Fee from their own wallet according to the estimate displayed by the wallet application. The Company is not liable for losses arising from gas spikes or volatility.

section5.title: 5. Third-Party Service Outages
section5.body: The Service depends on third-party providers including Pimlico (ERC-4337 bundler/paymaster), Alchemy (RPC), Vercel (hosting), wallet applications, and the blockchain networks themselves. The Company is not liable when the Service becomes wholly or partially unavailable, or when users incur losses, due to outages, suspensions, specification changes, deprecation, or performance degradation of these third-party services.

section6.title: 6. Changes in Laws and Regulatory Risk
section6.body: Crypto and blockchain-related laws and regulations may change in Japan and other jurisdictions. The Company is not liable for losses arising when the Service becomes wholly or partially unavailable due to changes in law, regulatory guidance, or compliance measures. Users are responsible for complying with laws applicable to their place of residence and use, and for confirming that their transactions through the Service are not illegal.

section7.title: 7. OpenPay Service Fee and Gas Sponsorship
section7.body: The OpenPay service fee is consideration for use of the Service, including payment processing, merchant QR code generation, the checkout UI, supported wallet integration, and operation and maintenance of the Service. For transactions in Gasless Payment mode, gas sponsorship and mitigation of network-fee volatility risk are additionally included in the consideration. The OpenPay service fee is not a pass-through of actual network fees (gas); the Company does not refund, charge additional amounts, or settle the difference between the displayed amount and the actual gas incurred. Once a transfer is finalized on-chain (including a transfer of the Network-Fee-equivalent in Gasless Payment mode), it cannot, in principle, be cancelled, refunded, or modified. In Standard Payment (with Gas) mode, the Company does not handle the Network Fee in any way; the Customer pays it from their own wallet.

section8.title: 8. Use during the Alpha Phase
section8.body: The Service is currently in alpha. Unexpected defects, display errors, transfer failures, wallet connection issues, specification changes to supported chains and tokens, third-party infrastructure outages, and similar events may occur. Before using the Service for real transactions, you must send small test amounts and confirm the destination wallet, amount, supported token, supported chain, payment mode, displayed fees, and the payment-completion flow.

Disclaimer.legalNote: This Disclaimer applies together with the Terms of Service. In case of conflict, the Terms of Service prevail. The Japanese version of this Disclaimer prevails over this English reference version.

Tokutei.title: Business Disclosure (Specified Commercial Transaction Act of Japan)
Tokutei.intro: This page is provided pursuant to Article 11 of the Specified Commercial Transaction Act of Japan and its enforcement regulations, disclosing business information of {company} (the "Company") concerning the blockchain payment service "{service}" (the "Service").

phone.label: Phone Number
phone.value: Omitted on this page. Pursuant to Article 23, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Enforcement Regulations of the Specified Commercial Transaction Act, we will disclose our phone number without delay by email or other means upon request.

serviceContent.label: Service Description
serviceContent.value: Non-custodial blockchain payment facilitation service, including generation of EIP-681 payment URIs and QR codes, batched user operations under ERC-4337, Tip widget, and gas relay. The Service never holds user funds. The Service supports two payment modes: "Gasless Payment" and "Standard Payment (with Gas)".

supportedTokens.label: Supported Tokens
supportedTokens.value: JPYC (an electronic payment instrument issued by JPYC Inc. as a funds transfer service provider registered under Japan's Payment Services Act), USDC (a stablecoin issued by Circle Internet Financial, Inc.), and other digital assets the Company may add from time to time. Supported tokens and chains may be added, changed, or suspended at the Company's discretion without prior notice.

price.label: Service Fee (OpenPay Service Fee)
price.value: The OpenPay service fee is free (0% of each transaction amount) during the alpha period. The Company does not charge any fee tied to the transaction amount (a percentage fee proportional to the amount). Costs per payment mode are as follows. (1) Gasless Payment mode: in paths where the Company sponsors the Network Fee (gas) (e.g. JPYC payments), the Company collects an amount equivalent to the Network Fee in JPYC or similar as recovery of that sponsored cost. That collected amount is a fixed amount based on the upper-bound (congestion-ceiling) price and is not tied to the transaction amount; the bearer (Customer or Merchant) may be configurable by the Merchant at QR code generation time (if the Merchant bears it, it is deducted from the Merchant's received amount). In paths where the Customer pays gas in a Supported Token (e.g. the ERC20 Paymaster for USDC), that fee is paid to the Paymaster provider and the Company does not collect it. (2) Standard Payment (with Gas) mode: the Company does not sponsor the Network Fee; the Customer pays it in the native token from their own wallet. Consideration for the services the Company provides (payment processing, merchant QR code generation, the checkout UI, supported wallet integration, and operation and maintenance of the Service) is free during the alpha period. Future charging is being considered along models not tied to the transaction amount, such as a monthly subscription or usage-license sales.

additionalFees.label: Additional Costs
additionalFees.value: (1) Network fees (gas): fees required for confirming transactions on the blockchain. In Gasless Payment mode, the user may be able to pay without separately holding native tokens such as POL or ETH. Specifically, in paths where the Company sponsors gas (e.g. JPYC payments) the Company advances the gas and collects an equivalent amount (a fixed amount based on the congestion-ceiling price) in JPYC or similar. In paths where the Customer pays gas in a Supported Token (e.g. the ERC20 Paymaster for USDC), the Customer pays the gas to the Paymaster provider in USDC or similar, and the Company does not collect it. In Standard Payment (with Gas) mode, the Customer pays the Network Fee in the native token (POL, ETH, etc.) from their own wallet. (2) Wallet application fees: governed by the terms of the wallet application chosen by the user. (3) Communication costs: internet connection charges and communication costs required to use the Service are borne by the user.

serviceStartTiming.label: Service Provision Timing
serviceStartTiming.value: Service to a Merchant begins when the Merchant connects a wallet and generates a QR code. Payment between Customer and Merchant is completed when the Customer scans the QR, approves the transfer in their wallet, and the transaction is finalized on-chain.

paymentTiming.label: Payment Timing and Method
paymentTiming.value: In Gasless Payment where the Company sponsors gas (e.g. JPYC payments), a Network-Fee-equivalent is transferred directly on-chain from the user's wallet to a wallet designated by the Company at the time each transaction is executed (where the Customer pays gas in a Supported Token, e.g. the ERC20 Paymaster for USDC, that fee is paid to the Paymaster provider and no transfer is made to a wallet designated by the Company; the OpenPay service fee is currently 0%, and if introduced in the future it will be transferred in the same manner). The Company does not receive, hold, manage, or later settle the price of goods, service fees, or other sales proceeds payable to Merchants. The Company does not issue separate invoices, hold funds in escrow, operate a prepaid charge system, or settle merchant sales.

returnPolicy.label: Refunds and Cancellations
returnPolicy.value: Due to the technical nature of blockchain, finalized transfers (including transfers of the price of goods and transfers of the Network-Fee-equivalent in Gasless Payment mode) cannot, in principle, be cancelled, refunded, or modified. The OpenPay service fee is consideration for use of the Service, including payment processing, gas sponsorship in Gasless Payment mode, and mitigation of network-fee volatility risk, and is, in principle, non-refundable after payment is completed. The Network-Fee-equivalent collected in Gasless Payment mode is likewise, as consideration for the Service (gas sponsorship), non-refundable after payment is completed, and the Company does not settle any difference between it and the actual gas incurred. Before submitting, users must verify the destination address, amount, supported token, supported chain, payment mode, OpenPay service fee, and bearer configuration. If the Service is unusable due to a material defect, please contact us by email; we will investigate and respond within a reasonable scope.

environment.label: Required Environment
environment.value: A wallet (EOA or smart contract account) capable of transacting on the supported blockchain (currently Polygon mainnet and others), supported token balance, and where applicable, network fees in the native token (e.g., POL), except for transactions in Gasless Payment mode where the Company sponsors the gas via Paymaster.
